title: Liver abscess (pus pocket in the liver)

items: A liver abscess is a pocket of pus in the liver, caused by bacteria or other germs.
Many people have no clear signs in the liver itself.
Fever is the most common sign.
Belly pain, weight loss, and sometimes yellow skin (jaundice).
Ultrasound or CT scan of the liver.
A needle sample of the pus for Gram stain and culture.
Blood cultures, blood sugar (HbA1c), and an amoeba antibody test.
Antibiotics are chosen based on the culture.
Drainage of the abscess is often needed, by needle or by a procedure.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Keep to all follow-up scans and blood tests.
Keep to the follow-up plan your team gives you.
Repeat scans show whether the abscess is shrinking.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Severe belly pain, or yellow skin that is getting worse
